record.original_question: Prove that any generalized minimal flow admits a background region B0 on which the vorticity is constant, with the remaining vorticity organized into blob regions separated from that background.

evidence.quote: Problem 15. For any GM-flow curl u = const in B0 . Thus, the level sets of curl u are of two sorts: real-analytic curves and entire domain B0 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider steady solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a compact analytic surface (or a planar domain) M with velocity field u and vorticity ω = curl u. A "generalized minimal (GM) flow" is a steady Euler flow that arises as a long-time weak limit of solutions to the 2D Euler equations and admits a decomposition M = B₀ ⊔ (⨆ᵢ Bᵢ), where the Bᵢ ("blob regions") are open sets bounded by streamlines, and B₀ ("background region") is the complement, with vorticity organized so that the level sets of ω inside each blob are real-analytic curves.

Prove the following structural statement: for any GM-flow, the vorticity ω = curl u is constant on the background region B₀. Equivalently, every level set of ω in M is either a real-analytic curve or coincides with the entire background region B₀.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an explicit open problem ("Problem 15") in a 2022/2023 preprint on generalized minimal flows. No subsequent work resolving the conjecture that vorticity is constant on the background region B₀ of any GM-flow was found.
